issues.cell: W1 and W3 x C2-C13 (adj l. 689, 691); the fixed-place sentence's 'A castle sited after the raised way' (adj l. 614-622); the bent-group list (adj l. 550-555); over the band at S6's end (adj l. 417-426); E-P4 (adj l. 1323-1330); base §4.8's castle (l. 7755-7757), §4.4's stage-k citadel (l. 5958-5960)
issues.claim: A castle's walls are fixed by S3 (8)'s claim, not pulled: the curtain is 'its own enceinte of kind bailey along the reservation polygon' (base l. 7755-7757), an inner ward's chain is S7's, and between an on_enceinte castle's weld vertices the trace 'is the bailey's outer arc itself' (base l. 5594-5595). No row lays them: W1 names S3's and S5a's traces; the bent group's list omits them while its definition ('every stretch laid by neither the pull nor a cost field') takes them in; the fixed-place sentence says a castle sited after a raised way is 'never reshaped', its filter testing only weld vertices and the town-side gate, and E-P4 names as standing only '(5)'s routes at generation, a held one at a regeneration'. Castle walls are laid after a raised way at every regeneration and New random under a held one (E-S3 regenerates 'a declared masonry aqueduct across a corner of a castle's bailey'), at a stage-k citadel beside S4's and S5b's viaducts, and at S6's end, where the claim stands but S7 has not laid the curtain, so whether S6's aqueduct and elevated road meet a standing wall is unsaid ((3) keeps supports off 'a reservation' only). Builders: the curtain bent locally (a castle reshaped), kept on its polygon through a held aqueduct's support (against item 110 (b)'s 'through an arch'), or every such claim rejected; at S6 an elevated road over a bailey built or not, a support in the curtain's outer half-band or not.

issues.cell: Strips, zones and nearest points: Footprints (adj l. 401-405, PRB7B-02); the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 602-613, 622-626); over the band's S6 read (adj l. 421-426); No gate and no tower (adj l. 524-534); base §4.4 S5a Trace (2)'s pin clause (l. 5948) and E-P9; E-S3's bar (adj l. 1130-1133); the sweep (adj l. 991)
issues.claim: Footprints reads a fixed place with 'the footprint of the gate or tower standing there' and says every text and bar reads it so (adj l. 403-405). At generation the steps that place things or keep clear of them run before any footprint stands: S3 (7)-(9) and S5a fix gates, river crossings and anchors; S6's aqueduct 'reads the fixed places ... before S7 lays their towers' and keeps its strip clear of 'the trace's gates'; S7 lays the towers and S10's step (0) builds the tower and gatehouse parts later (base l. 7705-7706, 7742-7745). The widths come later too: the grade is the step profile 'that S7 writes with the trace's furniture' (base l. 7710-7713), and the fixed-place zone's widening reads a glacis or berm the moat carve decides later. §4.4 S5a (2)'s 'a pin inside a raised way's under-deck strip moves along its arterial clear of it' is a point, untouched by E-P9 and pipeline's sweep. Builders: points tested at S3 (9), S5a and S6, then S7 and S10 (0) build an anchor tower or a gatehouse into the zone or strip, failing E-S3's '0 fixed places ... each with its footprint' and '0 gates' or towers' footprints in an under-deck strip', with no rule left to move a fixed place; or footprints and widths read from the rows they will be built by. A moved gate's move has no reach (the pull's 40 m band, §5.3's stage-1 distance bound), where fixed places are bounded by the trace's reach.

issues.cell: R7-03 (a): 'T and the boundary keep (5)'s routes and are not re-derived' (adj l. 848-849); base §4.2 S3 (6) (l. 5541-5553); S3 (7)'s harbour gate (l. 5570-5576); veto 17; E-S2 (adj l. 1098-1102)
issues.claim: S3 (6) computes T 'with the road multiplier 1/a1 ... on the lattice edges of (5)'s routes', and (5)'s routes are solved with S4's cost function, which prices viaducts. R7-03 (a)'s trigger - a route whose first point at T = t_1 lies on its deck - is the case where T runs cheaply out along that deck over the valley; the route is re-solved with no deck across the boundary, but T and the boundary keep the old routes. The stage-1 region then keeps ground only the dropped deck reached (a finger along the unbuilt deck over the valley, or the far rim as a second component), while no way goes there; the trace is pulled from it, stage 1's land counted on it, and T serves every later stage with a road that does not exist. Whether a priced deck edge is an edge of T's lattice is unstated. Builders: T over the deck (a wall following an unbuilt road across a valley, or a two-ring contour, F-WALL's 'does not close') or T on the ground beneath. The trigger also misses L*: the harbour gate is placed where L* first reaches T = t_1, L* a path of the tree (5) routes with, priced decks among its edges; R7-03 (a) re-solves only 'a route', so the harbour gate can stand on a valley floor beneath no deck.

issues.cell: 'beyond the foot': base §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 5948), beneath's pulled list (adj l. 476-478), W1's last cell (adj l. 689), the bent group's (i) (adj l. 577-578), Where the line crosses (adj l. 464-465); Line and band (adj l. 465-469); Footprints; R7-03 (a)'s trigger (adj l. 844-845); T110-2 (3)'s ramp case (base l. 18565-18567)
issues.claim: 'Beyond the foot' fixes no distance. Line and band keeps the line a band's half from a ramp, stair or foot, a lawful crossing keeps its band off them widened by the strip margin, and Footprints reads a gate by its gatehouse's footprint - but against strips and zones only, and ramps, stairs and feet are neither (the under-deck strip is 'over its piers and spans'). A pin just past the foot vertex, which S5a (2)'s words allow, lays the band over the foot and the gatehouse on the ramp, which T110-2 (3) bars for this very case ('no ramp, stair or foot in the band'). At stage 1 there is no rule: R7-03 (a) re-solves only a route whose first point at T = t_1 'lies on a raised stretch'; a first point on an end ramp or stair, or at the foot (a vertex on ground part 0), is a raised stretch for one builder and not another, and S3 (9) runs 'by S5a's rules', so a third moves S3's fixed gate beyond the foot at (9), after (8) and before (10)'s moat deck 'at every main gate' read it. Three gates, three traces.

issues.claim: E-D11's rung ends 'that stage left unwalled, reported (W_RAISED_MEETING)' and F-WALL runs at 'S3 (stage 1), S5a, S7'. At S3 it runs at (9), after (4) picked N1 gates by the walled law, (7) fixed them and the harbour gate, and (8) welded an on_enceinte castle whose outer arc 'becomes the stretch of town wall the castle shares'; then (10) carves the city moat 'along the (9) trace' with a deck at every main gate, (11) routes the harbour 'through a gate' with the trace impassable but at its gates, and S4 splits each gate route at its gate. The base defines an unwalled stage 1 only before its gates are picked (S3 (9) (a): 'walls nothing ... has no gate ... picked by the land law'). Builders keep N1 gate records with no wall, drop them, or re-pick by the land law; the on_enceinte castle is kept, re-sited or turned inside; the moat carved or not; the harbour route through a gate or not. At k >= 2 the rung runs after S5b spawned primaries to the walled N_k and with the stage's citadel welded. The rung is reachable at a first generation (E-S3's spur town with no clear rim point in reach) and at regenerations; E-S12 runs stage 2 only.

issues.cell: W3·C1, W3·C2, W3·C8 (adj l. 691); the way-and-channel lead and rows (a), (d) (adj l. 706, 722, 725); down before the wall (adj l. 443-446); base §7.2 Drawn constraints (l. 10819-10824); T110-2 (6) (base l. 18598-18607)
issues.claim: At a regeneration a held raised way stands before every stage; W3·C1 says 'a held way is not re-created' and W3·C2 lays 'the routes it is derived from ... after the held raised way and cross[es] it by §4.3's crossing rule (row a)', never along the strip. Nothing says what becomes of the route a held road deck belongs to: a locked generated viaduct (its reason key's a = 'the carried way's lineage') or a declared raised road. §7.2 re-routes arterials 'to reuse' drawn ways (on it); row (a) puts every route off it; the ledger counts the held key as standing (no second deck). Builders: (A) the re-solved route rides the held deck as its fixed stretch; (B) it meets it by row (a), re-solved elsewhere, the deck orphaned. S3 (6)'s T, S3 (7)'s gates, S5a's pins ('on a raised deck pins no gate') and S5b's c all differ; T110-2 (6)'s '(3)'s fixture re-derived from S4 with its viaduct locked - ... meeting it as in (3)' holds only under (A). Second, row (d) applies 'at a regeneration' and makes each spawned primary a main gate reaching N_k, while down before the wall sends a deck route across a held trace to a standing gate and makes a gate in a held wall by hand alone: under a held outer ring S5b makes a gate in it or falls short of N_k; E-S6 runs only a held stage-1 ring.

issues.cell: the fixed-place sentence's 'A raised way created after the wall' (adj l. 622-626) with PRB7B-03's town-side gate (adj l. 601-602) x V06 §3.19 (2)'s elevated-road endpoints (V06 l. 2774-2783); down before the wall (adj l. 447-450); C1 at S6's end; item 110 (b)
issues.claim: Item 110 (b) raises 'an ELEVATED ROAD linking two high wards, terraces or a citadel and a great temple over a lower district' (g l. 622-623). The base takes 'the citadel's reservation' as an endpoint, its anchor 'its highest part-0 way vertex inside it or on its boundary' (V06 l. 2776-2778), the course solved from P1 to P2 with both ends fixed. A citadel is a castle; its reservation is reached only at its town-side gate by the castle street, and S7's internal paths come after S6 - so at S6's end P1 is the castle street's vertex at the town-side gate, and at an epoch it may lie inside the bailey. PRB7B-03 made every castle's town-side gate a fixed place, and a raised way created after the wall keeps every fixed place outside its zone and off its ramps, stairs and feet, else (G3); a course from inside the bailey crosses the curtain and is not built. So no elevated road ever links a citadel: not built at generation, waiting at every epoch - the owner's named reason closed by a program reading. Builders: the endpoint never served; the road's own end exempted (its foot on the gate); or the anchor moved off the gate by a rule no text gives.
issues.required_change: Fixed-place sentence (adj l. 626), after 'every text that keeps a raised way's strip clear of fixed places means this zone (amended, PRB7-09).' add: 'A raised way whose own end serves a castle - an elevated road whose endpoint is a citadel's reservation (V06 §3.19 (2)) - ends outside it: its anchor is the castle street's highest vertex at which the road's feet, ramps and fixed-place zone keep the town-side gate, with its footprint, and the castle's wall strips clear, the castle street joining the foot to the gate on ground part 0, so the road neither stands on the gate nor crosses the curtain and the citadel's reason is served.' (ties by address); a citadel's, the highest vertex of its castle street outside the castle's wall strips at which the road's fixed-place zone keeps the town-side gate clear (§2.7's crossing table, the fixed-place sentence)'. E-S2 adds a METROPOLIS fixture whose elevated-road reading links its citadel and a great temple - built, its foot on the castle street clear of the town-side gate's fixed-place zone and the castle's wall strips, no part over the curtain.

issues.cell: R7-03 (b) (adj l. 861-869) x base §4.4 S5d's top-up (l. 6058-6068); W1·C2 at k >= 2; §4.8 Gates 'exactly N' (l. 7729); F-WALL's bars (l. 9203)
issues.claim: S5d's one top-up grows the level set 'to cover the shortfall, S5a re-traces only the affected arc between its pinned gates' (base l. 6064-6066). An arterial that crossed the stage's picked boundary on a deck has no pin, so it lies inside a re-traced arc, and the grown contour can cross it on its ground course beyond the deck's foot. R7-03 (b) keeps 'each arterial's crossing as the picked boundary had it ... at its pin, or under its deck', its ground course beyond each foot 'within the search band, impassable to the pull' - but the re-trace's boundary is the grown contour, crossing on the ground. Builders: a new gate (N_k + 1, against §4.8's 'exactly N' and F-WALL's 'main gates = N exactly'); a ground crossing with no gate (against '0 non-gate crossings'); or the arc held under the deck, the grown land beyond the foot not taken (and, where the foot lies beyond the grown contour's search band, the pull unable to reach under the deck). VEW-r6-01's closure does not reach this path; no clause runs a top-up on T110-2 (3)'s c14 fixture.
